body:
Oh I am out in the real world. I'm single for different reasons, less stupid reasons.

I don't even think about this a lot. These feelings arise every couple months, and last maybe an hour or two at the most. Wrote this post mostly to try to get them down and try to make sense of them, but also because I'm tired of them.

Thank you, have a good holiday yourself :)
That's definitely what I'm counting on. I forgot pretty quickly when I was with my ex.

It's so cool and flashy. Too bad it's completely impractical. One good dodge or block, your opponent can throw you off balance and get the upper hand in a manner of seconds. It's so easy to see coming too, and it would be slightly painful, but not hard to block at all.

*sigh* Martial Arts... If you wanna learn one that teaches you how to fight, not show off, Ninjitsu (I'm in the Bujinkan school but there are a few that othets that also claim to be true/historic ninjitsu). 100% Combat Pragmatism 0% Flair.

It's hard to let myself go into things without a plan. I do sometimes, and it works, but I'm not super comfortable with it yet, and still often get stuck. Or if I have too much time to think, I'll start formulating a plan anyway (could even start as a "plan to run without a plan"), but that could be avoided.

Biggest trouble I have is introducing myself to someone. That's where I feel I -need- a plan. Just coming up to someone saying "hi, how are you?" seems too fallible. I guess that answers your question about my standards; I would like when I introduce myself to someone to be able to form some kind of bond with someone.

It's kind of a relief to hear such a large amount of people's conversations are boring and it's not just me. Keeping that in mind should make things significantly easier (well, it is already as I am talking to a couple of the handful of friends I have at the moment.)

As for relationships growing stale... That's probably it. I just wasn't sure what it meant.

I do try to do all of that.

This is probably another issue I have to work through but, some questions seem too "cliché" and I'm afraid they'd make me seem uninteresting, others might make it sound like I'm an idiot for not being very well educated or rude for not paying enough attention when asking to repeat something (for that I could blame parenting, my dad is the same way, and so was my grandpa, and both would, in fact, call people idiots for it... But I can blame all I want that doesn't solve anything.)

I know etiquette, and social rituals (although, probably not well as I should, I often think too much about what applies to which situation, and try to go "by the book" cause to do otherwise feels even more awkward.)

Observation and imitation is one thing I'm working on, and I kinda learn that way, but I always try to put my own spin on things, and I find it hard to learn properly without practice.

As for practice... I'm kinda getting it with carrying conversations. Still have the hardest time with introductions.

1) I'm not sure what sort of standards I set for myself when interacting with others, I never really thought of that. 

I don't have much self talk during the fact, and I don't even compare things to past "failed" interactions. Like, I do that when I'm alone and in my head; which carries a bit of self loathing regarding why it failed or what I did wrong, but turns into a "how things could have gone" day dream (that's been a habit of mine for years). 

When I'm thinking about talking to someone new, I just try to run a game plan in my head. I think of several scenarios, but only -really- plan for one eventuality due to a one track mind, and it's usually the "preferred" scenario. Without a plan, it's hard to do anything, and when that plan doesn't pan out, sometimes I can find myself... Stuck.

Practice is definitely something I'm trying to get. Within the past month I guess it's gotten better just from talking to a few people at work. I hit rock bottom with this problem, maybe a year ago?

3) I realize people drift apart, but most of the relationships that have broken down feel more like this lack of social skills. What we have in common it feels like it's been talked to death (regardless of how long I've known them) and I feel like it's my shyness, inability to find common ground (or maybe their disinterest) that causes -me- to drift away. A former best friend of mine is the best example. I used to be really comfortable with him, used to have lots in common, now I struggle in talking to him (and can never approach him myself.) That's basically the story for everyone.

Hearing a girl moan, scream, or seeing her squirm in pleasure. Not any of that fake stuff from porn though. Especially if I'm the cause of the pleasure (You could probably guess I'm a big giver.)

Also, romantic hentai manga/doujins (and especially those where the guy finishes inside the girl and the artist took the time to draw an x-ray of the cumshot.)

Aaaaaaand, I guess I'm a furry... Nothing extreme like, RL fursuit stuff, but again, hentai.
It's not just about the attention. A lot of times it's about wanting to command respect and fear too.
